query: How can clinics improve triage and scheduling?

per_column.name: estimated_resource_intensity
per_column.rationale: A genuine new axis for triage/scheduling: grouping visits by resource load directly supports capacity planning. Values are reasonable inferences from clinical detail (labs, MRI, supportive care). Some subjectivity, e.g. MRI-ordered knee visit rated 'high' vs MI follow-up 'medium', but all readings are warranted by the text.

per_column.name: follow_up_required
per_column.rationale: Directly relevant to scheduling downstream appointments. Values track text: MI follow-up with 'repeat lipid panel in 3 months' = yes; viral URI 'return if worse' = yes (defensible); annual exam = no. Sound readings overall.

per_column.name: specialist_referral_needed
per_column.rationale: Useful for routing decisions in triage. Sampled values are consistent with text (none of the sampled visits explicitly initiate a new referral, so 'no' is a sound reading). Not redundant with other columns.

per_column.name: has_comorbidity
per_column.rationale: Comorbidity burden is a legitimate axis for triage risk stratification. Sampled 'no' values are defensible: prior MI is historical and arguably a comorbidity but text frames it as resolved; BMI 27 is not clearly flagged. Values are cautious rather than invented, so groundedness holds.

judge.rationale: All four added columns provide distinct, non-redundant axes (resource load, follow-up scheduling, referral routing, comorbidity risk) that meaningfully support the triage-and-scheduling query. Produced values in the evidence samples are sound readings or cautious inferences from the reason_for_visit text, with no invented facts or contradictions observed. Minor subjectivity in intensity/comorbidity labeling slightly tempers groundedness but does not amount to hallucination.
